newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on weather, fund selling.

text.p: A bearish weather forecast and aggressive fund selling, tied to long liquidation, knocked CBOT soybean futures to a lower close, traders said.
"The six- to 10-day was bearish and big fund selling was bearish," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. "There was commercial buying but it was scale-down buying and it didn't help much."

The National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook Wednesday was for normal to above normal temperatures and normal to below normal precipitation through most of the key U.S. soybean growing region from October 1 through October 5.
Private meteorologists said for the near term, Thursday and Friday, rain will push eastward across the U.S.
The rain will be followed by cooler temperatures, they said.
"We will be seeing cooler weather moving in after this front," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "It's not the knockout freeze people were looking for."
Soybeans rallied Wednesday on forecasts for frost late this week which could have damaged some of the soybean crop.
Soybeans closed 1/4 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down five at $7.90-3/4.
Fund selling Thursday totaled at least 15.0 million bushels with Refco Inc a key seller of ten million bushels of November and LIT America sold five million November, the traders said.
Commercial buying limited losses but there also was fund buying, they said.
"Rosenthal really moved the market. They bought eight million Nov beans and sold eleven million Dec corn," a trader said.
Rosenthal Collins bought eight million bushels of November, ADM Investor Services bought eight million November and Continental Grain bought two million November, they said.

Technicians pointed to sell stops which were hit near the open when November broke below chart support at $7.91-1/2. The next support level is $7.84-1/2 and the session low for November was $7.86-1/2 per bushel.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 50,000 contracts, up from 45,743 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, ADM Investor Services bought 1,000 November $8.00 calls and sold 1,000 November calls at six cents and bought 1,000 November $8.50 calls at 3-1/4 cents, the traders said.
Term Commodities bought 550 November $9.00 calls at 7/8 cent, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000, down from 21,951 Wednesday.
